pretreatments.description: Ozone pretreatment procedure: Grass particles (3 g) were adjusted for moisture (90% w/w) and placed into an enclosed stainless steel reactor with 1 cm bed height. Ozone was produced by a Pacific Ozone generator at 5.3% ozone concentration (w/w) using a flow rate of 2000 ml/min for 10 min. The reaction was performed at 100°C. Ozone dose was 0.79 g O_3/g TS.

Soaking aqueous ammonia (SAA) pretreatment procedure: Grass waste particles were soaked in a 28–30% (w/w) ammonium hydroxide solution for 24 hours at 50°C for 24 hours without agitation. The solid to liquid ratio was 2:10. The sample was washed twice thoroughly with distilled water to reach neutral pH, dried at 50°C, and used for further investigation.

Ozone combined with SAA (OSAA) pretreatment procedure: Grass waste particles were first treated with ozone for 10 min to deconstruct lignin, followed by SAA pretreatment for 6 hours at 50°C. The resulting material was used for further investigation.
Size reduction: Milled grass waste particles were sieved through a 42 mesh Tyler Standard Screen Scale to obtain grass waste particles with a size less than 0.354 mm.

Inoculum preparation: Anaerobic sludge containing a microbial community of hydrolyzing, acid-producing, acetate-producing, and methane-producing microbes was sampled from an anaerobic digester at the Pullman Wastewater Treatment Facility. The sludge had a concentration of 17.1 g TS/L (11.7 g VS/L) and pH of 7.5. It was used as inoculum for anaerobic tests.
